headline: Collaborative Storytelling Writing Game for ESL Classes
outcomes: Students contribute to a shared story, practising narrative writing and creative expression in English
Build sentence variety and coherence by connecting their contribution to what came before
Receive immediate AI feedback on grammar, vocabulary, and story logic in a low-stakes context
Develop listening and reading skills as students process each other's contributions
howItWorks: The AI generates a story starter related to your topic — a first sentence or short scene-setting paragraph
Each student adds one sentence to continue the story, submitted from their device
AI evaluates the sentence for grammar accuracy, coherence with the previous text, and creativity
The story grows on the classroom board in real time — the class can see the collective narrative develop
teacherUseCases: Creative writing warm-up that produces a complete class story in under 15 minutes
Narrative tense practice — students must match and extend a story already in past tense
End-of-topic activity where students write a story incorporating the unit's vocabulary

faq.q: How does the AI evaluate story contributions?
faq.a: The AI checks grammar accuracy, logical coherence with the previous sentence, and vocabulary richness. It gives feedback on all three dimensions so students understand what made their sentence strong or weak.

faq.q: What if a student writes something that doesn't fit the story?
faq.a: The AI flags incoherent contributions and the teacher can ask the student to revise before it's added to the story. The teacher has final say on what gets accepted.

faq.q: Can I specify a genre or setting?
faq.a: Yes. Type the topic as something like 'mystery story set in a hospital' or 'adventure in the mountains' and the AI will generate an appropriate starter and evaluate contributions against that genre.

faq.q: Is this better for individual or group work?
faq.a: Both work. In simultaneous mode everyone submits a sentence and the best one (by teacher choice or class vote) gets added. In turn mode each student adds one sentence in sequence.

faq.q: Do students write on their own devices?
faq.a: Yes — each student types their story sentence on their own phone or tablet in the browser. No download required; joining is as simple as opening the teacher's link.
Story Sprint is free to run. No subscription or student accounts required — students join via a browser link and start contributing within seconds.
